import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Number of opponent cells adjacent to the candidate that would flip (opp owner has <= my neighbours there), scaled."""
    moves = np.asarray(moves, dtype=int)
    N = owner.shape[0]
    # counts of my cells and opponent cells adjacent to each cell
    my_nb = adjacency[:, owner == 1].sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    opp_nb = adjacency[:, owner == -1].sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    # candidate becomes mine; for each opponent neighbour, count my neighbours after claim
    cand_adj = adjacency[moves]  # (k, N)
    # my neighbours of an opponent cell after claim = my_nb + (that opp cell is adjacent to candidate)
    my_after = my_nb[None, :] + cand_adj.astype(float)  # (k, N)
    opp_counts = opp_nb[None, :]  # broadcast
    is_opp = (owner == -1)[None, :]
    is_home_opp = np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)
    is_home_opp[homes[1]] = True
    flippable = is_opp & (~is_home_opp[None, :]) & (my_after >= opp_counts)
    # weight by points of flipped cells
    flips = (flippable * points[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    total_pts = points.sum()
    return flips / (total_pts + 1e-9)

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Fraction of the candidate's neighbours (after claiming it) that are empty, weighted by their points, minus a flip threat term."""
    k = len(moves)
    N = owner.shape[0]
    # build hypothetical owner after claiming each candidate
    # adjacency to candidate
    adj_c = adjacency[moves]  # (k, N) bool
    # neighbours of candidate
    deg = adj_c.sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    # empty neighbours (after claim they'd still be empty except the candidate itself)
    empty = (owner == 0)[None, :] & adj_c
    pts = points[None, :]
    empty_pts = (empty * pts).sum(axis=1)
    # potential flip: opponent neighbours of candidate that would flip if we claim it
    opp_nb = (owner == -1)[None, :] & adj_c
    # count our neighbours around each opponent neighbour (after claim, candidate is ours)
    # approximate: fraction of opponent-neighbour's neighbours that are ours (would be >= their count)
    # vectorised: for each candidate, sum over its opp neighbours of our_count / their_count margin
    ours_mat = (owner == 1).astype(float)
    opp_mat = (owner == -1).astype(float)
    # our support for each cell, plus candidate contribution
    support_ours = ours_mat @ adjacency.T.astype(float)  # (N,)
    support_opp = opp_mat @ adjacency.T.astype(float)
    # after claiming candidate, our support for its opp neighbours increases by 1 where adjacent
    # flip value: sum over opp neighbours of points * (support_ours+adj - support_opp >= 0)
    # compute per candidate
    # opp_nb is (k,N); support diff
    diff = (support_ours[None, :] + adj_c.astype(float)) - support_opp[None, :]  # (k,N)
    # only count opp neighbours (excluding home of opponent)
    mask = opp_nb.copy()
    mask[:, homes[1]] = False
    flippable = (mask & (diff >= 0))
    flip_pts = (flippable * pts).sum(axis=1)
    # empty density for expansion
    exp = empty_pts / (deg + 1.0)
    # normalise
    score = (exp + 0.5 * flip_pts / 5.0) / (1.0 + deg / 4.0)
    return score

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Points-denominated swing: how many opponent points are lost if this claim triggers flips, plus the cell's value, tempered by how many empty cells remain to be captured."""
    N = len(owner)
    my = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    opp_home = homes[1]
    # adjacent opponents that are NOT the home and not protected
    neigh = adjacency[moves]  # (k, N)
    opp_neigh = neigh & opp[None, :]
    opp_neigh[:, opp_home] = False
    # count how many of each opp neighbor's neighbours we already own (after claim: +1 from this move)
    my_count = my.astype(np.int32)
    opp_count = opp.astype(np.int32)
    # our neighbours per opponent cell (k, N) = for each candidate, for each cell, count of my neighbors of that cell
    my_neigh_of_cell = adjacency @ my_count  # (N,)
    opp_neigh_of_cell = adjacency @ opp_count  # (N,)
    # For a candidate m, the opponent cell j flips if: (my_neigh_of_cell[j] + adj[m,j]) >= opp_neigh_of_cell[j]
    adj_m = adjacency[moves].astype(np.int32)  # (k, N)
    my_after = my_neigh_of_cell[None, :] + adj_m  # (k, N)
    flips = opp_neigh & (my_after >= opp_neigh_of_cell[None, :])  # (k, N)
    swung = (flips * points[None, :]).sum(axis=1).astype(float)  # opponent points we flip
    # also our own cells at risk: opp cells next to candidate that could flip us later - skip
    val = points[moves].astype(float)
    # remaining empty cells fraction: early game flips matter more (more turns to exploit), late less
    empties = int((owner == 0).sum())
    total_claims = max(N - 2, 1)
    remaining = max(empties, 0) / total_claims
    # weight flips more when many turns remain; current cell value steady
    score = val / 5.0 + 2.0 * (swung / 5.0) * remaining
    return score

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Empty-neighbour count of the candidate, scaled by the board's mean empty degree (so it is not just the fraction)."""
    empty = (owner == 0)
    empt = (adjacency & empty[None, :]).sum(1)
    deg = adjacency.sum(1)

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Margin of my vs opponent influence after claiming, weighted by neighbour points and by whether flip counts tip."""
    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    A1 = (adjacency & mine[None, :]).sum(1).astype(float)
    Ao = (adjacency & theirs[None, :]).sum(1).astype(float)
    deg = adjacency.sum(1).astype(float)
    moves = np.asarray(moves, dtype=int)
    # after claiming candidate, my-neighbour count of every cell rises by 1 where adjacent
    cand_adj = adjacency[moves].astype(float)  # (k, N)
    my_after = A1[None, :] + cand_adj       # (k, N)
    # weighted margin: neighbours where I'd dominate (my_after >= Ao) count positive,
    # neighbours where opponent dominates count negative, weighted by their points
    margin = (my_after - Ao[None, :]) * points[None, :]
    # focus on cells near the candidate (its own neighbourhood)
    near = cand_adj > 0
    pos = np.where(near & (my_after >= Ao[None, :]), margin, 0.0).sum(1)
    neg = np.where(near & (my_after < Ao[None, :]), -margin, 0.0).sum(1)
    denom = np.maximum(deg[moves], 1) * 5.0
    values = (pos - neg) / denom
    return values

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Points flipped by this claim, discounted by how many of the flipped cells are cheap 1-pointers, plus a bonus for flips that empty the opponent's frontier (leaving them few empty neighbours)."""
    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    A1 = (adjacency & mine[None, :]).sum(1)
    Ao = (adjacency & theirs[None, :]).sum(1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    Aempty = (adjacency & empty[None, :]).sum(1)
    cand = adjacency[moves]
    opp_nb = cand & theirs[None, :]
    flip = opp_nb & (A1[None, :] + 1.0 >= Ao[None, :])
    flip[:, homes[1]] = False
    # value of flipped cells: weight 2/5-pointers more, 1-pointers less
    wt = np.where(points >= 5, 1.0, np.where(points == 2, 0.6, 0.25))
    base = (flip * wt[None, :]).sum(1)
    # after-flip frontier squeeze: opponent cells that were flipped take their empty-neighbour supply away
    # measure how much empty frontier the opponent loses relative to their remaining cells
    opp_remaining = theirs & ~flip
    opp_empty_after = (opp_remaining * Aempty[None, :]).sum(1)
    opp_empty_before = (theirs * Aempty[None, :]).sum(1)
    squeeze = (opp_empty_before - opp_empty_after) / np.maximum(opp_empty_before, 1.0)
    values = base / 5.0 + 0.5 * squeeze
    return values

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Tempo-scaled value: cell points weighted by how early (few claims left) plus a flip bonus for early grabs."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    total_claims = max(N - 2, 1)
    # fraction of the game still to be played (1 early -> 0 late)
    remaining = max(total_claims - turn, 0) / total_claims

    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    A1 = (adjacency & mine[None, :]).sum(1)
    Ao = (adjacency & theirs[None, :]).sum(1)

    cand = adjacency[moves]  # (k, N)
    opp_nb = cand & theirs[None, :]
    flippable = opp_nb & (A1[None, :] + 1.0 >= Ao[None, :])
    is_home_opp = np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)
    is_home_opp[homes[1]] = True
    flippable &= ~is_home_opp[None, :]
    flip_pts = (flippable * points[None, :]).sum(1)

    cell_pts = points[moves].astype(float)
    values = remaining * (cell_pts + 0.5 * flip_pts) / 15.0
    return values

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Vulnerability of the candidate: opponent pressure on it minus empty safety, weighted by its own point value."""
    moves = np.asarray(moves, dtype=int)
    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    A1 = (adjacency & mine[None, :]).sum(1).astype(float)
    Ao = (adjacency & theirs[None, :]).sum(1).astype(float)
    Ae = (adjacency & empty[None, :]).sum(1).astype(float)
    deg = np.maximum(adjacency.sum(1).astype(float), 1.0)
    # how contested the candidate is: opponent neighbours vs empty escape routes
    pressure = Ao[moves] / deg[moves]
    safety = Ae[moves] / deg[moves]
    # being surrounded by opponent near games end is dangerous; near-empty is fine
    remaining = max((owner.shape[0] - 2) - turn, 1)
    phase = 1.0 - remaining / max(owner.shape[0] - 2, 1)
    val = points[moves] / 5.0
    # high when valuable, contested, and late (flip risk on a high-value cell)
    values = val * (pressure - 0.5 * safety) * (0.5 + phase)
    return values

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative BFS graph distance from each candidate to the opponent's home, divided by N."""
    N = adjacency.shape[0]
    target = int(homes[1])
    dist = np.full(N, -1, dtype=np.int64)
    dist[target] = 0
    frontier = np.array([target], dtype=np.int64)
    while frontier.size > 0:
        # neighbours of the frontier not yet visited
        nb = adjacency[frontier].any(axis=0)
        nb[dist >= 0] = False
        nxt = np.nonzero(nb)[0]
        dist[nxt] = dist[frontier].min() + 1
        frontier = nxt
    d = dist[moves].astype(np.float64)
    d[d < 0] = N  # unreachable guard (should not happen on a connected board)
    return -d / float(N)

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Margin (my minus opponent neighbours) of each candidate after the claim, counted only over neighbours that are empty or enemy, weighted by their point value, normalised."""
    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    A1 = (adjacency & mine[None, :]).sum(1)
    Ao = (adjacency & theirs[None, :]).sum(1)
    # After claiming candidate c: my neighbours of cell j = A1[j] + adj[c,j]; opp neighbours unchanged.
    cand_adj = adjacency[moves].astype(np.float64)  # (k, N)
    margin = (A1[None, :] + cand_adj) - Ao[None, :]  # (k, N)
    # relevant cells: empty or opponent, not homes (homes never flip / never empty)
    relevant = ((owner == 0) | (owner == -1)).astype(np.float64)
    relevant[homes[0]] = 0.0
    relevant[homes[1]] = 0.0
    w = points.astype(np.float64) * relevant
    num = margin @ w  # (k,)
    den = cand_adj @ w + 1e-9
    return num / den

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative BFS distance from each candidate to the opponent's home, but weighted by the point value of the cells on that path's frontier: candidates whose short path to the enemy home runs through low-value empty cells are favoured (denial), normalised by N."""
    N = adjacency.shape[0]
    target = int(homes[1])
    dist = np.full(N, -1, dtype=np.int64)
    dist[target] = 0
    frontier = np.array([target], dtype=np.int64)
    while frontier.size > 0:
        nb = adjacency[frontier].any(axis=0)
        nb[dist >= 0] = False
        nxt = np.nonzero(nb)[0]
        dist[nxt] = dist[frontier].min() + 1
        frontier = nxt
    d = dist[moves].astype(np.float64)
    d[d < 0] = N
    # value of empty cells adjacent to each candidate, that lie on a shortest path toward opp home
    dist_all = dist.astype(np.float64)
    dist_all[dist_all < 0] = N
    # candidate's own distance to target
    dm = dist_all[moves]  # (k,)
    # for each candidate, average value of its empty neighbours that are closer to the target
    closer = (dist_all[None, :] < dm[:, None]) & (owner == 0)[None, :]
    nb_mask = adjacency[moves] & closer
    val = (nb_mask * points[None, :]).sum(1)
    cnt = nb_mask.sum(1)
    meanval = val / np.maximum(cnt, 1)
    # combine: favours being close (negative dist) and having low-value approach cells (denial of high-value path)
    return (-d / float(N)) * (0.5 + 0.5 * (1.0 - meanval / 5.0))

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Point-weighted safety margin of each candidate, but only counting neighbours that could still flip: empty or opponent-owned, weighted by their points, normalised by the candidate's own point value."""
    nb = adjacency[moves].astype(np.float64)          # (k, N)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)

    contestable = (~mine).astype(np.float64)
    my_p = nb @ (pts * mine)
    opp_p = nb @ (pts * theirs)
    empty_p = nb @ (pts * empty)
    # safety: my support vs the pressure/threat on the cell, weighted by the cell's own value
    own_val = pts[moves]
    support = my_p
    threat = opp_p + 0.5 * empty_p
    denom = support + threat + 1e-6
    values = (support - threat) / denom
    # emphasise it for high-value candidates so the optimiser can lean on 5-point cells
    return values * (0.5 + 0.5 * own_val / 5.0)

    moves = np.asarray(moves)
    owner = np.asarray(owner)
    points = np.asarray(points)
    adjacency = np.asarray(adjacency)
    opp_home = int(homes[1])

    # Neighbour counts before the claim
    mine = (owner == 1).astype(np.int32)
    opp = (owner == -1).astype(np.int32)
    my_nb = adjacency.astype(np.int32) @ mine          # (N,)
    opp_nb = adjacency.astype(np.int32) @ opp           # (N,)

    adj_c = adjacency[:, moves]                        # (N, k): x adjacent to candidate
    is_opp = (owner == -1)[:, None]                    # (N, 1)
    not_home = (np.arange(owner.shape[0]) != opp_home)[:, None]
    margin = (my_nb + 1 - opp_nb)[:, None]             # (N, 1)

    durable = flips & (margin >= 2)                    # (N, k)

    pts = points.astype(np.float64)[:, None]

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative BFS distance to the opponent's home, but the opponent's occupied cells are costly to pass through: distance computed on a graph where opponent-owned cells cost 3 steps per edge and empty cells cost 1, divided by N."""
    N = adjacency.shape[0]
    target = int(homes[1])
    opp = (owner == -1)
    # per-cell entry cost: stepping into an opponent cell is expensive (but its own home counts as 1)
    cost = np.where(opp, 3.0, 1.0)
    cost[target] = 1.0
    INF = 1e9
    dist = np.full(N, INF)
    dist[target] = 0.0
    visited = np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)
    # Dijkstra with vectorised frontier relaxation (no heapq allowed to loop over candidates)
    for _ in range(N):
        masked = np.where(visited, INF, dist)
        u = int(np.argmin(masked))
        if masked[u] >= INF:
            break
        visited[u] = True
        du = dist[u]
        nb = adjacency[u]
        cand_d = du + cost
        better = nb & (~visited) & (cand_d < dist)
        dist[better] = cand_d[better]
    d = dist[moves]
    d[d >= INF] = float(N)
    return -d / float(N)

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Points of empty cells that are opponent-reachable-only neighbours of the candidate, but excluding cells the opponent cannot reach before me (opponent distance to cell <= my distance-from-home to cell), scaled by 15."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    empty = (owner == 0)

    # BFS distances from my home and from the opponent's home
    def bfs(src):
        dist = np.full(N, -1, dtype=np.int64)
        dist[src] = 0
        frontier = np.array([src], dtype=np.int64)
        while frontier.size > 0:
            nb = adjacency[frontier].any(axis=0)
            nb[dist >= 0] = False
            nxt = np.nonzero(nb)[0]
            dist[nxt] = dist[frontier].min() + 1
            frontier = nxt
        return dist

    d_me = bfs(int(homes[0])).astype(np.float64)
    d_opp = bfs(int(homes[1])).astype(np.float64)
    d_me[d_me < 0] = N
    d_opp[d_opp < 0] = N

    opp_reach = empty & (adjacency @ (owner == -1).astype(np.int64) > 0)
    mine_reach = empty & (adjacency @ (owner == 1).astype(np.int64) > 0)
    # only cells the opponent can plausibly grab before me (it's ahead on the race to that cell)
    race_win = d_opp <= d_me + 1
    deniable = opp_reach & ~mine_reach & race_win

    weighted = points.astype(np.float64) * deniable.astype(np.float64)
    return (adjacency[moves].astype(np.float64) @ weighted) / 15.0

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Number of empty cells that would become mine-only or opponent-only reachable as a result of this claim: change in my exclusive frontier minus opponent's, normalised by N."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    empty = (owner == 0)
    my_adj = adjacency & (owner == 1)[None, :]
    opp_adj = adjacency & (owner == -1)[None, :]
    my_reach = empty & (my_adj.sum(1) > 0)
    opp_reach = empty & (opp_adj.sum(1) > 0)

    # for each candidate: recompute reachability after claim + flips
    my_nb = my_adj.sum(1)
    opp_nb = opp_adj.sum(1)
    k = moves.shape[0]
    out = np.empty(k, dtype=float)
    idx_all = np.arange(N)
    for i, c in enumerate(moves):
        adj_c = adjacency[c]
        # flips: opponent cells adjacent to c, not home, where my count after claim >= opp count
        flippable = (owner == -1) & adj_c & (idx_all != homes[1]) & (my_nb + 1 >= opp_nb)
        new_owner = owner.copy()
        new_owner[c] = 1
        new_owner[flippable] = 1
        new_empty = (new_owner == 0)
        nm = new_empty & (adjacency[:, new_owner == 1].sum(1) > 0)
        no = new_empty & (adjacency[:, new_owner == -1].sum(1) > 0)
        # exclusive frontier change
        my_only = (nm & ~no).sum() - (my_reach & ~opp_reach).sum()
        opp_only = (no & ~nm).sum() - (opp_reach & ~my_reach).sum()
        out[i] = (my_only - opp_only) / float(N)
    return out

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative (normalised) best one-ply grab value available to the opponent after my claim and its flips."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    my_home = homes[0]
    opp_home = homes[1]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)

    out = np.zeros(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)
    for idx in range(moves.shape[0]):
        c = moves[idx]
        # flips: opponent cells adjacent to c, not opp home, with A1[j]+1 >= Ao[j]
        adj_c = adjacency[c]
        flips = adj_c & opp & (np.arange(N) != opp_home) & ((A1 + 1) >= Ao)
        mine2 = mine.copy()
        mine2[c] = True
        mine2 |= flips
        opp2 = opp & ~flips
        A1b = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
        Aob = adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)
        legal_e = empty & (Aob > 0)
        if not legal_e.any():
            out[idx] = 0.0
            continue
        # gain[e] = points[e] + sum over j adjacent to e with mine2[j], j != my home, Aob[j]+1 >= A1b[j]
        flip_back_mask = mine2 & (np.arange(N) != my_home) & ((Aob + 1) >= A1b)
        flip_back_pts = np.where(flip_back_mask, pts, 0.0)
        # for each empty e: sum of flip_back_pts over neighbours
        gain = pts + adjacency @ flip_back_pts
        best = gain[legal_e].max()

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative BFS distance to opponent home, but measured only through empty cells and gated to the early game (distance ignored once the frontier reaches the enemy home)."""
    N = adjacency.shape[0]
    target = int(homes[1])
    # BFS over empty cells only (my claimed cells and opp territory are barriers unless target itself)
    dist = np.full(N, -1, dtype=np.int64)
    dist[target] = 0
    frontier = np.array([target], dtype=np.int64)
    passable = (owner == 0)
    passable[target] = True
    while frontier.size > 0:
        nb = adjacency[frontier].any(axis=0)
        nb[dist >= 0] = False
        nb &= passable
        nxt = np.nonzero(nb)[0]
        if nxt.size == 0:
            break
        dist[nxt] = dist[frontier].min() + 1
        frontier = nxt
    d = dist[moves].astype(np.float64)
    d[d < 0] = N
    # fraction of claims made so far
    total_claims = float(N - 2)
    prog = turn / max(total_claims, 1.0)
    # early-game emphasis: full weight at start, decaying as game progresses
    gate = max(0.0, 1.0 - prog)
    return gate * (-d / float(N))

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative expected points I would lose if the opponent claims an empty neighbour that can flip the candidate: points at risk (candidate plus exposed cells) times a capped threat count, normalised by 30."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    k = moves.shape[0]
    my = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    opp_home = int(homes[1])
    my_home = int(homes[0])
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)

    A1 = adjacency @ my.astype(np.int64)          # my neighbours per cell
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)         # opp neighbours per cell
    Aadj = adjacency.astype(np.int64)

    adj_c = adjacency[moves]                       # (k, N)

    not_opp_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_opp_home[opp_home] = False
    not_my_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_my_home[my_home] = False

    # flips after my claim of c (opp cells adjacent to c, not opp home, A1+1 >= Ao)
    flips = adj_c & opp[None, :] & not_opp_home[None, :] & ((A1[None, :] + 1) >= Ao[None, :])
    f_nb = flips.astype(np.int64)
    n_my = A1[moves] + f_nb.sum(axis=1)
    n_opp = Ao[moves] - f_nb.sum(axis=1)

    # opponent cells remaining after my flips, and their neighbour counts
    opp2 = opp[None, :] & ~flips
    Aob = opp2.astype(np.int64) @ Aadj             # (k, N)

    # empty threat cells adjacent to c from which opponent could flip c
    threat = (empty[None, :] & adj_c & (Aob > 0)
              & ((n_opp + 1) >= n_my)[:, None])    # (k, N)

    # my cells after my claim (mine plus the candidate c)
    owned_after = np.zeros((k, N), dtype=bool)
    owned_after |= my[None, :]
    if k > 0:
        owned_after[np.arange(k), moves] = True

    # number of threat cells adjacent to each cell
    threat_nb = threat.astype(np.int64) @ Aadj     # (k, N)

    A1_after = A1[None, :] + adj_c                 # (k, N): +1 at candidate
    can_flip_my = owned_after & (threat_nb > 0) & ((Aob + 1) >= A1_after) & not_my_home[None, :]

    at_risk_pts = (can_flip_my.astype(np.float64) * pts[None, :]).sum(axis=1)   # (k,)

    tcount = np.minimum(threat.sum(axis=1), 3).astype(np.float64)
    value = -(at_risk_pts / 30.0) * (tcount / 3.0)
    return value

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative expected one-ply grab value for the opponent after my claim, using a soft-average over their legal claims weighted by threat, minus my protected-cell count (normalised)."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    my_home = int(homes[0])
    opp_home = int(homes[1])
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    not_my_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_my_home[my_home] = False
    not_opp_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_opp_home[opp_home] = False

    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)

    k = moves.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    for idx in range(k):
        c = int(moves[idx])
        adj_c = adjacency[c]
        flips = adj_c & opp & not_opp_home & ((A1 + 1) >= Ao)
        mine2 = mine.copy()
        mine2[c] = True
        mine2 |= flips
        opp2 = opp & ~flips
        A1b = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
        Aob = adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)

        legal = empty & (Aob > 0)
        if legal.any():
            # opponent claim value: points gained + my cells it would flip back
            flip_back = mine2 & not_my_home & ((Aob + 1) >= A1b)
            flip_back_pts = np.where(flip_back, pts, 0.0)
            gain_all = pts + adjacency @ flip_back_pts
            gains = gain_all[legal]
            # vulnerability of each opponent claim: how many of MY cells it threatens
            # (opponent claims adjacent to more of my cells are more dangerous — use count)
            threat_count = (adjacency[legal] & mine2[None, :]).sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)
            weights = np.exp(0.7 * threat_count - 0.7 * threat_count.max())
            expected = float((gains * weights).sum() / (weights.sum() + 1e-9))
        else:
            expected = 0.0

        # how many of my cells are safe from a single opponent flip next turn (protected):
        # my cells j with A1b[j] > Aob[j] + 1 (can't be flipped by any single opp claim)
        safe = mine2 & not_my_home & (A1b > Aob + 1)
        protected_pts = float((pts * safe).sum())

        out[idx] = -expected / 30.0 + 0.5 * (protected_pts / 30.0)
    return out

    N = owner.shape[0]

    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)

    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)

    Aob = (opp[None, :] & ~flips).astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64)  # opp neighbours after

    N = owner.shape[0]

        nbrs &= (dBFS < 0)
        frontier = np.nonzero(nbrs)[0]
        dBFS[frontier] = d
    maxd = int(dBFS.max()) if (dBFS >= 0).any() else 0
    dBFS = np.where(dBFS < 0, maxd + 1, dBFS)

    k = moves.shape[0]

        c = int(moves[idx])
        new_owner = owner.copy()
        new_owner[c] = 1
        nbrs = np.nonzero(adjacency[c])[0]

            opp_count = int(np.sum(new_owner[jn] == -1))

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Points of opponent cells this claim would flip, minus the points of my own non-home cells the opponent could flip back on its next claim (net flip balance), /15."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    my_home = homes[0]
    opp_home = homes[1]
    not_opp_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool); not_opp_home[opp_home] = False
    not_my_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool); not_my_home[my_home] = False

    adj_moves = adjacency[moves]                      # (k, N)
    is_opp = opp[None, :] & not_opp_home[None, :]
    flip = adj_moves & is_opp & (A1[None, :] + 1 >= Ao[None, :])   # (k, N)
    gain = (flip * pts[None, :]).sum(1)

    # after my claim + flips: my neighbours per cell and opp neighbours per cell
    A1b = A1[None, :] + adj_moves.astype(np.int64) + flip.astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64)
    Aob = Ao[None, :] - flip.astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64)

    # for each empty cell e the opponent could legally claim, the cells it would flip back
    legal_e = empty[None, :] & (Aob > 0)              # (k, N)
    my_vuln = mine[None, :] & not_my_home[None, :] & (Aob[:, :, None] + 1 >= A1b[:, :, None]) if False else None
    # vectorised: for each candidate, for each empty e, my cells j adjacent to e that flip back
    # flipback[k,e,j] = legal_e[k,e] & adj[e,j] & mine[j] & not home & (Aob[k,j]+1 >= A1b[k,j])
    adj_j = adjacency[None, :, :]                     # (1, N, N) e x j
    mymask = (mine & not_my_home)[None, None, :]      # (1,1,N)
    cond_j = (Aob[:, None, :] + 1 >= A1b[:, None, :]) # (k,1,N) per j
    fb = legal_e[:, :, None] & adj_j & mymask & cond_j  # (k, N_e, N_j)
    # best loss: opponent picks the e maximizing points flipped back
    loss_per_e = (fb * pts[None, None, :]).sum(2)     # (k, N)
    loss = loss_per_e.max(1)

    return (gain - loss) / 15.0

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative of the opponent's best two-ply swing after my claim: their best immediate grab value minus the value I can claw back on my next claim, summed over their top grabs (normalised by 30)."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    my_home = homes[0]
    opp_home = homes[1]
    mine0 = (owner == 1)
    opp0 = (owner == -1)
    empty0 = (owner == 0)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine0.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp0.astype(np.int64)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    not_my_home = np.arange(N) != my_home
    not_opp_home = np.arange(N) != opp_home

    out = np.zeros(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)
    for idx in range(moves.shape[0]):
        c = moves[idx]
        adj_c = adjacency[c]
        flips = adj_c & opp0 & not_opp_home & ((A1 + 1) >= Ao)
        mine1 = mine0.copy()
        mine1[c] = True
        mine1 |= flips
        opp1 = opp0 & ~flips
        A1b = adjacency @ mine1.astype(np.int64)
        Aob = adjacency @ opp1.astype(np.int64)
        empty1 = empty0.copy()
        empty1[c] = False
        empty1 |= flips  # flipped cells are no longer empty
        empty1 &= ~mine1

        legal_e = empty1 & (Aob > 0)
        if not legal_e.any():
            out[idx] = 0.0
            continue

        # opponent grab gain at each legal empty e (one ply)
        flip_back_mask = mine1 & not_my_home & ((Aob[None, :] if False else Aob) + 1 >= A1b)
        flip_back_pts = np.where(flip_back_mask, pts, 0.0)
        gain = pts + adjacency @ flip_back_pts  # opponent's value of grabbing each cell
        legal_idx = np.nonzero(legal_e)[0]
        vals = gain[legal_idx]

        # consider top opponents grabs (up to 2) and subtract what I could reclaim
        order = np.argsort(-vals)[:2]
        total_threat = 0.0
        for oi in order:
            e = legal_idx[oi]
            v = vals[oi]
            # after opp claims e: simulate flips of my cells adjacent to e
            opp_ne = adjacency[e]
            # my cells that would flip to opp
            flips_to_opp = opp_ne & mine1 & not_my_home & ((Aob + 1) >= (A1b + 1 - 0))
            # more precisely: opponent neighbours of j after their claim = Aob[j] + (adj e-j), mine = A1b[j]
            Aob_after = Aob + opp_ne.astype(np.int64)
            flips_to_opp = opp_ne & mine1 & not_my_home & (Aob_after >= A1b)
            mine2 = mine1 & ~flips_to_opp
            opp2 = opp1.copy()
            opp2[e] = True
            opp2 |= flips_to_opp

            # my best reclaim next turn: value of an empty cell I can grab, plus flips of opp cells
            empty2 = empty1.copy()
            empty2[e] = False
            empty2 &= ~mine2
            mine_nb = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
            opp_nb = adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)
            legal_m = empty2 & (mine_nb > 0)
            if legal_m.any():
                adjm = adjacency[legal_m]
                opp_cells = opp2[None, :]
                flippable = adjm & opp_cells & not_opp_home[None, :] & (mine_nb[None, :] + 1 >= opp_nb[None, :])
                reclaim = pts[legal_m] + (flippable * pts[None, :]).sum(1)
                best_reclaim = reclaim.max()
            else:
                best_reclaim = 0.0
            total_threat += v - best_reclaim

        out[idx] = -total_threat / 30.0
    return out
features.measures: Negative of the opponent's best two-ply swing after my claim: their best immediate grab value minus the value I can claw back on my next claim, summed over their top grabs (normalised by 30).

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Net flip swing: points I would flip by claiming minus the best points the opponent could flip back on their reply, /30."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    A = adjacency.astype(np.float64)

    A1 = A @ mine.astype(np.float64)
    Ao = A @ opp.astype(np.float64)
    idx = np.arange(N)
    home1 = int(homes[0])
    home2 = int(homes[1])

    adj_c = adjacency[moves]  # (k, N)

    # my flips: neighbor is opponent's, not their home, and after my claim A1+1 >= Ao
    flips = adj_c & opp[None, :] & (idx[None, :] != home2) & ((A1[None, :] + 1) >= Ao[None, :])
    gain = (flips * pts[None, :]).sum(1)

    # board after my claim + flips
    mine2 = mine[None, :] | (adj_c & empty[None, :])  # (k, N)
    opp2 = opp[None, :] & ~flips                       # (k, N)
    A1b = mine2.astype(np.float64) @ A                  # (k, N)
    Aob = opp2.astype(np.float64) @ A                   # (k, N)

    # opponent's legal claims after my move
    claimed_by_me = adj_c & empty[None, :]
    legal_e = empty[None, :] & (Aob > 0) & ~claimed_by_me  # (k, N)

    # which of my cells the opponent could flip on reply (if they claim a neighbour)
    flippable_mine = mine2 & (idx[None, :] != home1) & ((Aob + 1) >= A1b)  # (k, N)
    flippable_pts = flippable_mine * pts[None, :]  # (k, N)

    # reply gain for each opponent claim e = sum_{j adj e} flippable_pts[j]
    gain_all = flippable_pts @ A  # (k, N)
    best_reply = np.where(legal_e, gain_all, -1.0).max(axis=1)
    best_reply = np.maximum(best_reply, 0.0)

    return (gain - best_reply) / 30.0

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Points of empty cells exactly two claims away, weighted by how many of my future-branch step-1 cells also touch them (a contested-reach mass), minus the same for the opponent's two-step reach, /30."""
    E = (owner == 0)
    N = owner.shape[0]
    Af = adjacency.astype(np.float64)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)

    # my two-step reach (cells empty, 2 hops from any of my cells, not 1 hop), counting multiplicity
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    my1 = E & (Af @ mine.astype(np.float64) > 0)
    my2_count = (Af @ my1.astype(np.float64)) * E.astype(np.float64)
    my2_count[my1] = 0.0
    opp1 = E & (Af @ opp.astype(np.float64) > 0)
    opp2_count = (Af @ opp1.astype(np.float64)) * E.astype(np.float64)
    opp2_count[opp1] = 0.0

    A = adjacency[moves].astype(np.float64)  # (k, N)
    # step1 empty neighbours of each candidate
    s1 = A * E[None, :]
    # step2 multiplicity reachable from candidate via empty step1 cells (excluding c and step1)
    s2_count = s1 @ Af  # (k, N) multiplicity
    s2_count *= E[None, :]
    s2_count *= (1.0 - s1) * (1.0 - A)
    # contested reach: how many of my current branches also reach it (proxy for contest/coverage)
    reach = s2_count * (1.0 + my2_count[None, :])

    mine_reach_val = (reach * pts[None, :]).sum(1)
    opp_deny_val = (s2_count * opp2_count[None, :] * pts[None, :]).sum(1)
    values = (mine_reach_val - opp_deny_val) / 30.0
    return values

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative expected points lost next turn: probability-like ratio (opp claimable empty neighbours / their neighbours) times my value at risk after my claim and flips, /30."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    my = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    my_home = homes[0]
    opp_home = homes[1]
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    Af = adjacency.astype(np.float64)

    A1 = adjacency @ my.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)

    adj_c = adjacency[moves]                                   # (k, N)
    not_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_home[opp_home] = False
    flip_cond = (A1[None, :] + 1 >= Ao[None, :])
    flips = adj_c & opp[None, :] & not_home[None, :] & flip_cond   # (k, N)
    f_nb = flips.astype(np.int64)

    n_my = A1[moves] + f_nb.sum(axis=1)                        # (k,)
    # after my claim, my territory including c and flips
    mine2 = my[None, :] | (np.arange(N)[None, :] == moves[:, None]) | flips  # (k, N)
    opp2 = opp[None, :] & ~flips                               # (k, N)

    # my cells at risk: my2 cells (not home) that opponent could flip by claiming an empty nb
    # opponent claims empty e adjacent to some opp2 cell; e's nbrs set flips
    A1b = mine2.astype(np.float64) @ Af                        # (k, N) my neighbours per cell after claim
    Aob = opp2.astype(np.float64) @ Af                         # (k, N) opp neighbours per cell after claim

    # empty cells the opponent can claim next: adjacent to opp2
    opp_legal = empty[None, :] & (Aob > 0)                     # (k, N)
    # a my-cell j is flippable by claim e if j adjacent to e, j != my_home, Aob[e]+1 >= A1b[j]
    # for each empty e, sum of pts of my cells it would flip
    flippable_mask = mine2 & (np.arange(N)[None, :] != my_home) & ((Aob + 1) >= A1b)  # (k, N)
    flip_pts = np.where(flippable_mask, pts[None, :], 0.0)     # (k, N)
    # exposure[e] = points of my cells that empty e would flip
    exposure = flip_pts @ adjacency.T                          # (k, N)
    # expected loss: sum over legal opponent claims of exposure, weighted down by how many legal claims exist
    n_legal = opp_legal.sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)         # (k,)
    total_exp = (exposure * opp_legal).sum(axis=1)             # (k,)
    # opponent picks the best, so use max exposure among legal claims (bounded by mean + max blend)
    masked = np.where(opp_legal, exposure, -1.0)
    best_exp = masked.max(axis=1)
    best_exp = np.maximum(best_exp, 0.0)
    # blend best and average to smooth
    avg_exp = total_exp / np.maximum(n_legal, 1.0)
    risk = 0.5 * best_exp + 0.5 * avg_exp
    return -risk / 30.0

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):

    opp_nb = cand & (owner == -1)[None, :]

    my_count_after = A1[None, :] + 1.0
    opp_count_after = np.maximum(Ao[None, :] - 1.0, 0.0)

    margin = my_count_after - opp_count_after

    values = (flip * w * points[None, :]).sum(1) / 15.0
    return -values

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Net swing: points of opponent cells this claim would flip, minus the points of my own non-home cells that become vulnerable to being flipped back by the opponent's best immediate reply."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    not_my_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_my_home[homes[0]] = False
    not_opp_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_opp_home[homes[1]] = False

    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)

    adj_c = adjacency[moves]                      # (k, N)
    flip = adj_c & opp[None, :] & not_opp_home[None, :] & (A1[None, :] + 1 >= Ao[None, :])
    flip_pts = (flip * pts[None, :]).sum(1)       # (k,)

    # after claiming c and flips: my cells and opponent cells
    mine2 = mine[None, :] | (np.arange(N)[None, :] == moves[:, None]) | flip   # (k, N)
    opp2 = opp[None, :] & ~flip                                                # (k, N)
    A1b = mine2.astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64)                  # (k, N)
    Aob = opp2.astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64)                   # (k, N)

    # opponent legal replies: empty cells adjacent to opp2
    legal = empty[None, :] & (Aob > 0)                                          # (k, N)

    # For each possible opponent reply e, it flips my non-home cells j adjacent to e
    # with Aob[j] + 1 >= A1b[j]. The damage of reply e = points[e]? No: points of my cells it flips.
    # flip_back per (cand, j, e) is too big; compute per candidate the max over legal e of damage.
    # damage[e] = sum_j adjacency[e,j] * vulnerable_j, vulnerable_j = my non-home, Aob[j]+1>=A1b[j]
    vuln = mine2 & not_my_home[None, :] & (Aob + 1 >= A1b)                      # (k, N)
    vuln_pts = vuln.astype(np.float64) * pts[None, :]                          # (k, N)
    # damage over opponent replies: (k, N_empty) = adjacency @ vuln_pts  (only meaningful at legal e)
    damage = vuln_pts @ adjacency.astype(np.float64)                           # (k, N) damage if reply at cell e
    damage = np.where(legal, damage, 0.0)
    worst = damage.max(axis=1)                                                 # (k,)

    return (flip_pts - 0.5 * worst) / 15.0

    N = owner.shape[0]
    idx = np.arange(N)
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1) & (idx != homes[1])
    E = (owner == 0)
    k = moves.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=float)

        mine1 = mine.copy()
        mine1[c] = True

        flipped = np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)
        nbrs_c = adjacency[c]
        cand_opp = nbrs_c & opp
        if cand_opp.any():

            o = (adjacency[js] & opp[None, :]).sum(axis=1)

        myA = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
        oppA = adjacency @ (opp & ~flipped).astype(np.int64)

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Net flip balance spread over the opponent's best reply: points I would flip now minus the points the opponent's single best flip-back could take, scaled by how much of the game is left, /15."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    my_home = homes[0]
    opp_home = homes[1]
    not_my_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool); not_my_home[my_home] = False
    not_opp_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool); not_opp_home[opp_home] = False

    adj_moves = adjacency[moves]
    is_opp = opp[None, :] & not_opp_home[None, :]
    flip = adj_moves & is_opp & (A1[None, :] + 1 >= Ao[None, :])
    gain = (flip * pts[None, :]).sum(1)

    A1b = A1[None, :] + adj_moves.astype(np.int64) + flip.astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64)
    Aob = Ao[None, :] - flip.astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64)

    legal_e = empty[None, :] & (Aob > 0) & ~adj_moves
    adj_j = adjacency[None, :, :]
    mymask = (mine & not_my_home)[None, None, :]
    cond_j = (Aob[:, None, :] + 1 >= A1b[:, None, :])
    fb = legal_e[:, :, None] & adj_j & mymask & cond_j
    loss_per_e = (fb * pts[None, None, :]).sum(2)
    loss = loss_per_e.max(1)

    # spread: how many distinct empty cells offer a profitable flip-back (0..3), as a "breadth" measure
    profitable = (loss_per_e > 0).sum(1).astype(np.float64)
    breadth = np.minimum(profitable, 3.0) / 3.0

    # remaining-game weighting: early claims are less costly to expose than late ones
    remaining = max(N - 2 - turn, 0)
    frac = remaining / float(max(N - 2, 1))

    net = (gain - loss) / 15.0
    # amplify net when many flip-back options exist (opponent has choices), damp when game nearly over
    return net * (0.5 + 0.5 * breadth) * (0.3 + 0.7 * frac)

    Aob = (opp_rem.astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64))  # (k, N)

    my_rem = mine[None, :] | flippable                         # my cells (including newly flipped) per candidate

    # empty cells adjacent to remaining opp territory (opp can claim there)
    opp_frontier = empty[None, :] & (adj_c & opp_rem).any(axis=0)[None, :] & (opp_rem @ adjacency.astype(np.int64) > 0)
    # (k, N) : empty cell e that opp can claim now (adjacent to opp_rem)
    opp_legal = empty[None, :] & (opp_rem.astype(np.int64) @ adjacency.astype(np.int64) > 0)

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Weighted margin (my minus opponent neighbours after the claim) over empty/enemy non-home neighbours, signed by whether the margin is on our side of flipping, normalised by weighted adjacency count."""
    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    A1 = (adjacency & mine[None, :]).sum(1)
    Ao = (adjacency & theirs[None, :]).sum(1)
    cand_adj = adjacency[moves]
    margin = (A1[None, :] + cand_adj.astype(np.float64)) - Ao[None, :]
    relevant = ((owner == 0) | (owner == -1))
    relevant[homes[0]] = False
    relevant[homes[1]] = False
    w = points.astype(np.float64) * relevant.astype(np.float64)
    # nonlinearity: squashing the margin so that being safely above 0 matters little,
    # being just at the flip boundary matters a lot, being below matters negatively.
    # use tanh of margin, and emphasize the boundary crossings.
    squashed = np.tanh(margin)
    # also give extra weight to cells that are exactly at boundary (margin in {0,1}) since they are flip-flippable
    boundary = np.exp(-np.abs(margin - 0.5))
    weight = w[None, :] * (0.5 * squashed + 0.5 * boundary)
    num = (cand_adj.astype(np.float64) * weight).sum(1)
    den = (cand_adj.astype(np.float64) * w[None, :]).sum(1) + 1e-9
    return num / den

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """For each candidate: points of the opponent-free pocket it opens into, but only the part of that pocket that is strictly closer (in free-cell steps) to the candidate than to the opponent's nearest territory; divided by 30."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    empty = (owner == 0)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    A = adjacency

    # opponent distance (BFS over all cells, step cost 1) from opponent territory
    INF = float(N + 5)
    d_opp = np.full(N, INF)
    d_opp[opp] = 0.0
    frontier = opp.copy()
    step = 0
    while frontier.any():
        step += 1
        nb = (A @ frontier.astype(np.int64)) > 0
        nb &= (d_opp == INF)
        if not nb.any():
            break
        d_opp[nb] = step
        frontier = nb

    # free pocket cells: empty with no opponent neighbour (safe to walk into)
    Ao = A @ opp.astype(np.int64)
    free = empty & (Ao == 0)

    out = np.zeros(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)
    idx_all = np.arange(N)
    for i, c in enumerate(moves):
        if not free[c]:
            continue
        # BFS over free cells starting from c, distance in free-steps
        dfree = np.full(N, INF)
        dfree[c] = 0.0
        frontier = np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)
        frontier[c] = True
        step = 0
        while frontier.any():
            step += 1
            nb = (A @ frontier.astype(np.int64)) > 0
            nb &= free & (dfree == INF)
            if not nb.any():
                break
            dfree[nb] = step
            frontier = nb
        # pocket cells: free cells reached, plus c itself
        in_pocket = (dfree < INF)
        # rival distance from c to that cell through open/empty graph (upper bound on opponent arrival)
        # opponent arrival to a pocket cell j: d_opp[j] (in open steps) ; we compare free-steps from c vs opp open-steps
        closer = in_pocket & (dfree < d_opp)
        # exclude the candidate cell itself from the mass (it is claimed, not a future gain)
        mass_mask = closer & (idx_all != c)
        out[i] = pts[mass_mask].sum() / 30.0
    return out

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Tempo-weighted value of cells the opponent can claim next turn (their best immediate flip-count), negative, normalised."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)

    # cells adjacent to my territory that could be flipped by an opponent claim

    not_opp_home[homes[1]] = False
    my_flippable = mine & not_opp_home & (Ao + 1 >= A1)

    # empty cells the opponent could claim (adjacent to opp territory)
    opp_legal = empty & (Ao > 0)

    if not opp_legal.any():
        return np.zeros(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)

    # For each opponent-legal empty cell e, the value it could grab: points[e] + points of my flippable neighbours
    flippable_pts = np.where(my_flippable, pts, 0.0)
    grab_value = pts + adjacency @ flippable_pts  # (N,)
    best_opp_grab = grab_value[opp_legal].max() if opp_legal.any() else 0.0

    # For each candidate: does claiming it reduce that best threat? Estimate post-claim best opp grab.
    out = np.empty(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)
    for i, c in enumerate(moves):

        flips = adj_c & opp & not_opp_home & ((A1 + 1) >= Ao)
        mine2 = mine.copy(); mine2[c] = True; mine2 |= flips
        opp2 = opp & ~flips
        A1b = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
        Aob = adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)
        empty2 = empty & ~(np.arange(N) == c)
        opp_legal2 = empty2 & (Aob > 0)
        if not opp_legal2.any():
            out[i] = best_opp_grab
            continue
        my_flip2 = mine2 & not_opp_home & (Aob + 1 >= A1b)
        fp2 = np.where(my_flip2, pts, 0.0)
        gv2 = pts + adjacency @ fp2
        out[i] = gv2[opp_legal2].max()
    return -(out - best_opp_grab) / 15.0

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Sum over cells flipped by this claim of points[j] * min(post-flip owner-neighbour margin, 3), /15."""
    moves = np.asarray(moves, dtype=int)
    adj = adjacency.astype(np.int32)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp_home = int(homes[1])

    # Neighbour counts before the claim
    A1 = adj @ mine.astype(np.int32)          # my neighbours per cell
    Ao = adj @ opp.astype(np.int32)           # opponent neighbours per cell

    # Candidate rows
    adj_c = adj[moves]                        # (k, N)
    A1_c = A1[moves]                          # (k,)
    Ao_c = Ao[moves]

    # Flipped set F: opponent cells adjacent to c, not opp home, with A1+1 >= Ao
    is_opp = opp[None, :] & (np.arange(adj.shape[0])[None, :] != opp_home)
    F = adj_c.astype(bool) & is_opp & ((A1_c[:, None] + 1) >= Ao_c[:, None])  # (k, N)
    Ff = F.astype(np.int32)

    # A1' = A1 + adj[c] + F@adjacency ; Ao' = Ao - F@adjacency
    A1p = A1[None, :] + adj_c + Ff @ adj
    Aop = Ao[None, :] - Ff @ adj

    return vals / 15.0

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Exclusive 5-point-cell access race: sum over 5-point empty cells j of 5/(1+D[c,j]) for D<=3 and D<d_opp[j], /15, only when no candidate can flip anything."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    k = moves.shape[0]
    empty = (owner == 0)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    mine = (owner == 1)

    # Opponent adjacency counts (Ao) and my adjacency counts (A1) per cell.
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int32)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int32)

    # Flippable pairs: opponent non-home cells adjacent to a candidate with A1+1 >= Ao.
    opp_home = homes[1]
    nonhome_opp = opp.copy()
    nonhome_opp[opp_home] = False
    # For each candidate c, count opponent non-home neighbours that would flip.
    # A cell x flips if adjacency[c,x] and nonhome_opp[x] and A1[x]+1 >= Ao[x].
    flippable_cell = nonhome_opp & ((A1 + 1) >= Ao)
    # candidates adjacent to any flippable cell
    adj_to_flippable = adjacency[:, flippable_cell].any(axis=1) if flippable_cell.any() else np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)
    total_flippable = int(adj_to_flippable[moves].sum())

    if total_flippable != 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    # d_opp: BFS through empty cells only, starting from empty cells adjacent to opponent.
    d_opp = np.full(N, 99, dtype=np.int32)
    frontier = empty & (Ao > 0)
    d_opp[frontier] = 1
    for step in range(2, 5):
        # expand: empty cells adjacent to current frontier, not yet reached
        nbr = (adjacency @ frontier.astype(np.int32)) > 0
        new = empty & nbr & (d_opp == 99)
        d_opp[new] = step
        frontier = new
        if not new.any():
            break

    # 5-point empty cells
    five = empty & (points == 5)
    five_idx = np.where(five)[0]

    if five_idx.size == 0:
        return np.zeros(k)

    # D: per candidate BFS through empty cells, steps 1..3.
    # D shape (k, N)
    D = np.full((k, N), 99, dtype=np.int32)
    D[np.arange(k), moves] = 0
    frontier = np.zeros((k, N), dtype=bool)
    frontier[np.arange(k), moves] = True
    for step in range(1, 4):
        nbr = (frontier.astype(np.int32) @ adjacency.T) > 0  # (k, N)
        new = empty[None, :] & nbr & (D == 99)
        D[new] = step
        frontier = new
        if not new.any():
            break

    # value = sum_j 5/(1+D[:,j]) for D<=3 and D < d_opp[j]
    Dj = D[:, five_idx].astype(np.float64)  # (k, m)
    dopp_j = d_opp[five_idx].astype(np.float64)  # (m,)
    mask = (Dj <= 3) & (Dj < dopp_j[None, :])
    contrib = np.where(mask, 5.0 / (1.0 + Dj), 0.0)
    value = contrib.sum(axis=1) / 15.0
    return value

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative best opponent follow-up *net* value after my claim and flips (their gain minus my flip-back recovery), /30."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    my_home = homes[0]
    opp_home = homes[1]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    idx_arr = np.arange(N)

    out = np.zeros(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)
    for idx in range(moves.shape[0]):
        c = moves[idx]
        adj_c = adjacency[c]
        flips = adj_c & opp & (idx_arr != opp_home) & ((A1 + 1) >= Ao)
        mine2 = mine.copy()
        mine2[c] = True
        mine2 |= flips
        opp2 = opp & ~flips
        A1b = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
        Aob = adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)
        legal_e = empty & (Aob > 0)
        if not legal_e.any():
            out[idx] = 0.0
            continue
        # opponent's grab: which of my cells would they flip after claiming e?
        my_flippable = mine2 & (idx_arr != my_home) & ((Aob + 1) >= A1b)  # (N,)
        my_flip_pts = np.where(my_flippable, pts, 0.0)
        # gross gain for opponent = points[e] + points of my cells flipped by e
        gross = pts + adjacency @ my_flip_pts
        # my counter-recovery: my cells adjacent to e that are NOT flipped, could be re-flipped by me next turn
        # approximate: value of my cells adjacent to e that survive (not flipped) weighted by fragility
        survive = mine2 & ~my_flippable & (idx_arr != my_home)
        fragile_pts = np.where(survive, pts, 0.0)
        exposed = adjacency @ fragile_pts  # my surviving-but-adjacent value
        net = gross - 0.5 * exposed  # opponent net of grab minus my residual exposure value
        best = net[legal_e].max()
        out[idx] = -best / 30.0
    return out

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Per adjacent opponent cell, points * (1 if it flips, else -my_neighbour_deficit * opp_share) so near-miss cells I dominate locally are penalised when flipping is far, /15."""

    cand = adjacency[moves]
    opp_nb = cand & (owner == -1)[None, :]
    margin = (A1[None, :] + 1.0) - Ao[None, :]        # >=0 -> flips now
    # how far I am from flipping: deficit when negative
    deficit = np.maximum(-margin, 0.0)
    # my local share of the neighbourhood of that opp cell
    share = A1[None, :] / np.maximum(A1[None, :] + Ao[None, :], 1.0)
    # flips count +1; near-miss cells are discounted by how badly I already dominate them
    # (a cell I already surround heavily but can't flip is a poor target vs one on the edge)
    prox = np.where(margin >= 0.0, 1.0, share / (1.0 + deficit))
    w = opp_nb.astype(np.float64) * prox * points[None, :].astype(np.float64)
    w[:, homes[1]] = 0.0
    return w.sum(1) / 15.0

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Valued boundary tension: for each candidate, weighted sum over its non-home neighbours of points * (flip-margin gap to the flip threshold), squared and signed by whether my claim pushes the cell toward flipping, using the true per-cell threshold (A1+1 >= Ao), normalised by total adjacent points."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    A1 = (adjacency & mine[None, :]).sum(1).astype(np.float64)
    Ao = (adjacency & theirs[None, :]).sum(1).astype(np.float64)
    cand_adj = adjacency[moves].astype(np.float64)  # (k, N)

    # after claiming c, the neighbour counts change: c adds +1 to A1 of every adjacent cell
    # flip condition for enemy cell j: A1[j]+1 >= Ao[j]  -> after +1 for claimed c, threshold gap
    # gap = (A1 + 1) - Ao  ; gap>=0 means flippable. Also relevant for empty cells: how close
    # the opponent would be to flipping it back (Ao+1 >= A1+1) etc. Use symmetric tension:
    # for enemy-owned cells: gap_e = (A1 + adj[c]) - Ao  (they flip when >=0)
    # for empty cells: gap_o = (Ao) - (A1 + adj[c])      (opponent flips them later when >=... )
    adj_c = cand_adj  # (k, N) whether c adjacent to j

    # enemy cells: margin toward being flipped by my claim
    gap_enemy = (A1[None, :] + adj_c) - Ao[None, :]          # (k, N)
    # empty cells: once I own c, my pressure vs theirs; margin toward me being able to keep/flip
    gap_empty = (A1[None, :] + adj_c) - Ao[None, :]

    is_enemy = (theirs)[None, :] & (adj_c > 0)
    is_empty = (owner == 0)[None, :] & (adj_c > 0)
    # exclude homes
    is_enemy[:, homes[0]] = False
    is_enemy[:, homes[1]] = False
    is_empty[:, homes[0]] = False
    is_empty[:, homes[1]] = False

    w = points.astype(np.float64)[None, :]

    # squashed margin: emphasise the boundary (gap near 0), saturate far from it.
    # signed: positive when margin is on my side (I flip them / I out-pressure them)
    squash = np.tanh(gap_enemy / 1.5)
    # extra sharp bonus exactly at the flip boundary (gap in {0,1})
    boundary = np.exp(-np.abs(gap_enemy - 0.5))

    enemy_term = np.where(is_enemy, w * (0.6 * squash + 0.4 * boundary), 0.0).sum(1)
    empty_term = np.where(is_empty, w * np.tanh(gap_empty / 2.0), 0.0).sum(1)

    den = (np.where(is_enemy, w, 0.0).sum(1) + np.where(is_empty, w, 0.0).sum(1)) + 1e-9
    return (enemy_term + 0.5 * empty_term) / den

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Gate * (points of empty cells reachable in exactly two claims from the candidate, excluding step-1 cells and the candidate, that have no opponent neighbour) / 30, with gate = 1/(1+F), F = opponent non-home cells flippable by some candidate now; the two-step value is additionally weighted by each target cell's own flip-resistance (1/(1+flippable-neighbour count)) so candidates differ within the same gate."""
    N = len(owner)
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)

    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)

    not_opp_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_opp_home[homes[1]] = False

    cand_adj = adjacency[moves]  # (k, N)
    flippable = opp & not_opp_home & (A1 + 1 >= Ao)
    any_cand = cand_adj.any(0)
    F = float((flippable & any_cand).sum())
    gate = 1.0 / (1.0 + F)

    nb1 = cand_adj & empty[None, :]
    E = (adjacency & empty[None, :]).astype(np.float64)
    raw2 = nb1.astype(np.float64) @ E  # path counts of length 2 through empties
    reach2 = (raw2 > 0) & empty[None, :] & ~nb1 & ~cand_adj
    k = len(moves)
    onehot = np.zeros((k, N), dtype=bool)
    onehot[np.arange(k), moves] = True
    reach2 &= ~onehot

    no_opp_nb = (Ao == 0)
    excl = reach2 & no_opp_nb[None, :]

    # per-cell flip-resistance weight: how many opponent cells could flip this empty cell
    # if I owned it (i.e. opponent neighbours that would then be outnumbered).
    # Use opponent-neighbour count as a proxy for how contested the cell is.
    opp_nb_count = Ao.astype(np.float64)  # opponent neighbours per cell
    resist = 1.0 / (1.0 + opp_nb_count)   # (N,)

    weighted = excl * (pts[None, :] * resist[None, :])
    val = weighted.sum(1) / 30.0
    return gate * val

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative sum over the opponent's best *two* one-ply grabs after my claim and its flips (each normalised by 30), i.e. how much value the opponent can extract in their next two moves."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    my_home = homes[0]
    opp_home = homes[1]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    idx_all = np.arange(N)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)

    k = moves.shape[0]
    out = np.zeros(k, dtype=np.float64)
    for i in range(k):
        c = moves[i]
        adj_c = adjacency[c]
        flips = adj_c & opp & (idx_all != opp_home) & ((A1 + 1) >= Ao)
        mine2 = mine.copy()
        mine2[c] = True
        mine2 |= flips
        opp2 = opp & ~flips
        A1b = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
        Aob = adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)
        legal_e = empty & (Aob > 0)
        if not legal_e.any():
            out[i] = 0.0
            continue
        flip_back_mask = mine2 & (idx_all != my_home) & ((Aob + 1) >= A1b)
        flip_back_pts = np.where(flip_back_mask, pts, 0.0)
        gain = pts + adjacency @ flip_back_pts
        legal_idx = np.nonzero(legal_e)[0]
        # best and second best grabs
        if legal_idx.size == 1:
            best = gain[legal_idx[0]]
            second = 0.0
        else:
            g = gain[legal_idx]
            order = np.argsort(-g)
            best = g[order[0]]
            second = g[order[1]]
        out[i] = -(best + second) / 30.0
    return out
features.measures: Negative sum over the opponent's best *two* one-ply grabs after my claim and its flips (each normalised by 30), i.e. how much value the opponent can extract in their next two moves.

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Opponent cells adjacent to the candidate, weighted by points and by how exposed they are to a *future* flip (already-flipping cells discounted, since f006 handles them), using the opponent cell's own degree as a normaliser so high-degree enemy cells are harder to crack, /15."""
    A1 = (adjacency & (owner == 1)[None, :]).sum(1).astype(np.float64)
    Ao = (adjacency & (owner == -1)[None, :]).sum(1).astype(np.float64)
    deg = adjacency.sum(1).astype(np.float64)
    cand = adjacency[moves]
    opp_nb = cand & (owner == -1)[None, :]
    # margin: how far each adjacent opp cell is from flipping after this claim
    margin = (A1[None, :] + 1.0) - Ao[None, :]
    # already-flipping (margin>=0) -> 0 (f006 covers those); near-miss (margin<0) -> partial credit
    # scaled by how many neighbours that opp cell has: a high-degree cell has more slack.
    slack = np.maximum(deg[None, :] - Ao[None, :], 1.0)
    prox = np.where(margin >= 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 / (1.0 + (-margin)))
    w = opp_nb.astype(np.float64) * prox * points[None, :].astype(np.float64) / slack
    w[:, homes[1]] = 0.0
    return w.sum(1) / 15.0

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Sum over opponent neighbours j of c of points[j] * convertibility[j,c] / (1 + deficit[j]), /15, where convertibility counts only empty neighbours e of j that are NOT already supported by my territory but become supported by claiming c (the follow-through claim exists)."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    theirs = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)

    A1 = (adjacency & mine[None, :]).sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)   # my neighbours per cell
    Ao = (adjacency & theirs[None, :]).sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)  # opp neighbours per cell

    cand = adjacency[moves]                       # (k, N)
    opp_nb = cand & theirs[None, :]               # (k, N)
    opp_nb[:, homes[1]] = False

    # deficit: extra my-supporters still needed after claiming c
    d = np.maximum(0.0, Ao - A1 - 1.0)            # (N,)

    # Only count empty neighbours e of j that are NOT already supported by my territory
    # but ARE adjacent to c: these are the genuine follow-through claims that convert j.
    base_sup = (A1 > 0)                           # (N,)
    empty_f = empty.astype(np.float64)
    base_f = base_sup.astype(np.float64)
    unsup_empty = empty_f * (1.0 - base_f)        # (N,)

    # conv[j,k] = # empty neighbours e of j with unsup_empty[e] and adjacency[moves[k], e]
    weighted_adj = adjacency * unsup_empty[None, :]   # (N, N)
    conv = weighted_adj @ cand.T.astype(np.float64)   # (N, k)

    weight = (opp_nb.T.astype(np.float64) * points[:, None]) / (1.0 + d[:, None])  # (N, k)
    value = (weight * conv).sum(axis=0) / 15.0        # (k,)
    return value

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Tempo-weighted net flip ledger: (1-f)*G - f*B, f = remaining/(N-2), G = points I flip now /15, B = opponent's best one-ply flip-back value /15."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    rem = max(0, (N - 2) - turn)
    f = rem / max(1, N - 2)

    moves = np.asarray(moves)
    k = moves.shape[0]
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    adj = adjacency

    # Neighbour counts before claim
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    A1 = adj[:, mine].sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)   # my neighbours per cell
    Ao = adj[:, opp].sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)    # opp neighbours per cell

    opp_home = homes[1]

    # G: points of opponent non-home cells flipped by claiming each move
    G = np.zeros(k)
    # B: opponent's best one-ply grab value after my claim + flips
    B = np.zeros(k)

    for idx in range(k):
        c = moves[idx]
        # After claim: c becomes mine
        A1_after = A1.copy()
        Ao_after = Ao.copy()
        # c's neighbours: for each neighbour j of c, my count increases by 1
        nbrs_c = adj[c]
        A1_after[nbrs_c] += 1.0
        # c itself is now mine; its own counts don't matter for flip test of others
        # Determine flips: opponent cells adjacent to c, non-home, with A1_after[j] >= Ao_after[j]
        flip_mask = nbrs_c & opp & (np.arange(N) != opp_home) & (A1_after >= Ao_after)
        G[idx] = pts[flip_mask].sum()

        # Apply flips: flipped cells become mine
        flipped = flip_mask
        # Update ownership after claim + flips
        owner_after = owner.copy()
        owner_after[c] = 1
        owner_after[flipped] = 1

        # Recompute neighbour counts after claim+flips
        mine_after = (owner_after == 1)
        opp_after = (owner_after == -1)
        A1_new = adj[:, mine_after].sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)
        Ao_new = adj[:, opp_after].sum(axis=1).astype(np.float64)

        # Empty cells adjacent to one of my cells after claim
        empty = (owner_after == 0)
        my_cells = np.where(mine_after)[0]
        adj_to_mine = adj[:, my_cells].any(axis=1) if my_cells.size > 0 else np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)
        candidates_e = empty & adj_to_mine

        if not candidates_e.any():
            B[idx] = 0.0
            continue

        # For each such empty cell e, opponent claims it: e becomes opp
        # Then flips: my non-home cells adjacent to e with Ao_new[j]+1 >= A1_new[j]
        e_idx = np.where(candidates_e)[0]
        my_home = homes[0]
        best = 0.0
        for e in e_idx:
            nbrs_e = adj[e]
            # after opp claims e, opp count for neighbours of e increases by 1
            Ao_e = Ao_new.copy()
            Ao_e[nbrs_e] += 1.0
            flip_mask_e = nbrs_e & mine_after & (np.arange(N) != my_home) & (Ao_e >= A1_new)
            val = pts[flip_mask_e].sum()
            if val > best:
                best = val
        B[idx] = best

    G = G / 15.0
    B = B / 15.0
    return (1.0 - f) * G - f * B

idea.hypothesis: A flip's worth depends on how many claims remain to undo it: early flips are transient while the opponent's reply is imminent, late flips are final. All tried net-flip features are static, so they cannot express this. Writing G (points I flip now) with weight (elapsed/(N-2)) and B (the opponent's best one-ply flip-back value after my claim) with weight (remaining/(N-2)) makes the trade-off shift over the game, which the fixed-weight span of f006 and f031 cannot reproduce. import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative opponent follow-up swing: best (points grabbed + my points flipped back) over opponent claims after mine, minus my gain from the claim itself, /30, only counting opponent claims that would actually flip one of my cells."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    my_home = int(homes[0])
    opp_home = int(homes[1])
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    idx_all = np.arange(N)
    not_my_home = idx_all != my_home
    not_opp_home = idx_all != opp_home
    Af = adjacency.astype(np.float64)

    out = np.zeros(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)
    for idx in range(moves.shape[0]):
        c = moves[idx]
        adj_c = adjacency[c]
        flips = adj_c & opp & not_opp_home & ((A1 + 1) >= Ao)
        my_gain = pts[c] + pts[flips].sum()
        mine2 = mine.copy()
        mine2[c] = True
        mine2 |= flips
        opp2 = opp & ~flips
        A1b = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
        Aob = adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)
        legal_e = empty & (Aob > 0)
        if not legal_e.any():
            out[idx] = 0.0
            continue
        # cells of mine2 that opponent could flip back
        flip_back_mask = mine2 & not_my_home & ((Aob + 1) >= A1b)
        flip_back_pts = np.where(flip_back_mask, pts, 0.0)
        # opponent swing for claiming e: pts[e] + my flipped-back points adjacent to e
        gain = pts + Af @ flip_back_pts
        # only consider opponent claims that flip something of mine (aggressive grabs)
        flips_any = (Af @ flip_back_mask.astype(np.float64)) > 0
        aggressive = legal_e & flips_any
        if aggressive.any():
            best = gain[aggressive].max()
        else:
            best = 0.0
        out[idx] = -(best - my_gain) / 30.0
    return out

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative, per candidate, of the points at risk if the opponent claims its best-flipping empty neighbour next turn: for every empty cell adjacent to the candidate, simulate the opponent claiming it, sum the points of my cells it would flip, take the best (worst for me), /15. Zero if no such threat exists."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    my = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    my_home = homes[0]
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)

    A1 = adjacency @ my.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)

    adj_c = adjacency[moves]                      # (k, N) neighbours of each candidate
    threat_cells = adj_c & empty[None, :]         # (k, N) empty cells opponent could grab next to c
    # restrict to cells the opponent can actually claim (adjacent to some opp cell)
    reachable = (Ao > 0)
    threat_cells = threat_cells & reachable[None, :]

    # For each (candidate, threat cell e): which of MY cells would flip if opp claims e.
    # opp claims e: Ao[j] + 1 >= A1[j]  for my cell j adjacent to e, j != my home.
    not_home = np.ones(N, dtype=bool)
    not_home[my_home] = False
    flip_cond_my = ((Ao[None, :] + 1) >= A1[None, :]) & my[None, :] & not_home[None, :]  # (1,N) which my cells would flip given e adjacent
    # flip_pts_vec[j] = points[j] if my[j] and flips
    flip_pts_vec = np.where(flip_cond_my[0], pts, 0.0)   # (N,)

    # For each candidate c and each threat cell e adjacent to c: value = sum over my neighbours of e of flip_pts_vec
    # = (adjacency @ flip_pts_vec)[e] summed over e in threat_cells[c]
    cell_flip_value = adjacency.astype(np.float64) @ flip_pts_vec   # (N,) points lost if opp claims each cell
    cell_flip_value = cell_flip_value * (~ (np.arange(N) == my_home))

    # best threat per candidate: max over e in threat_cells[c] of cell_flip_value[e]
    masked = np.where(threat_cells, cell_flip_value[None, :], -1.0)
    best = masked.max(axis=1)
    best = np.where(best < 0.0, 0.0, best)
    return -best / 15.0

import numpy as np

def feature(moves, owner, homes, points, adjacency, turn):
    """Negative of the points of the single highest-value empty cell that the opponent could claim next turn and that would flip one of my cells, divided by 5 — measures the worst immediate retaliation available to the opponent, only late in the game."""
    N = owner.shape[0]
    mine = (owner == 1)
    opp = (owner == -1)
    empty = (owner == 0)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)
    my_home = homes[0]

    # My cells vulnerable to flipping: not my home, and opponent already has >= my count - 1 neighbours
    A1 = adjacency @ mine.astype(np.int64)
    Ao = adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)
    vulnerable = mine & (np.arange(N) != my_home) & (Ao + 1 >= A1)

    if not vulnerable.any():
        return np.zeros(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)

    # For each empty cell e the opponent could claim (adjacent to opp territory),
    # which vulnerable cells would flip? A vulnerable cell j flips from e iff e is its neighbour
    # and after opp claims e: Ao[j]+1 >= A1[j] (already true by vulnerability).
    # Value of the retaliation = points of j (lost) captured via claiming e.
    # So value[e] = sum of points of vulnerable neighbours of e.
    vuln_pts = np.where(vulnerable, pts, 0.0)
    # opp-legal empties: empty cells adjacent to opponent territory
    opp_legal = empty & ((adjacency @ opp.astype(np.int64)) > 0)
    # retaliation value per empty cell
    retal = adjacency @ vuln_pts  # sum of vulnerable-neighbour points
    retal = np.where(opp_legal, retal, 0.0)

    # For each candidate: after my claim+flips, would reduce the opponent's opportunities.
    # Approximate: my claim removes one empty cell (the candidate) and flips some opp cells.
    # Score = -(worst retaliation remaining after my claim) / 5
    A1f = A1.astype(np.float64)
    Aof = Ao.astype(np.float64)
    not_home_mask = (np.arange(N) != homes[1])

    out = np.zeros(moves.shape[0], dtype=np.float64)
    for i, c in enumerate(moves):
        adj_c = adjacency[c]
        # flips from claiming c
        flips = adj_c & opp & not_home_mask & (A1f + 1.0 >= Aof)
        # after my claim: mine2, opp2
        mine2 = mine | flips
        mine2[c] = True
        opp2 = opp & ~flips
        # recompute vulnerability
        A1b = adjacency @ mine2.astype(np.int64)
        Aob = adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)
        vuln2 = mine2 & (np.arange(N) != my_home) & (Aob + 1 >= A1b)
        vuln2_pts = np.where(vuln2, pts, 0.0)
        opp_legal2 = empty & ~np.eye(N, dtype=bool)[c] & ((adjacency @ opp2.astype(np.int64)) > 0)
        # opp_legal2: empty, not c, adjacent to opp2
        retal2 = adjacency @ vuln2_pts
        retal2 = np.where(opp_legal2, retal2, 0.0)
        worst = retal2.max() if retal2.size else 0.0
        out[i] = -worst / 5.0
    return out

    adj_m = adjacency[moves]                 # (k, N)
    pts = points.astype(np.float64)

    # flipped[c,j]: opponent cell j (not opp home) adjacent to c, flips after my claim
    is_opp = opp[None, :] & (np.arange(N)[None, :] != opp_home)
    flips = adj_m & is_opp & ((A1[None, :] + 1) >= Ao[None, :])   # (k, N)

    # after claim: my count of j = A1[j] + adj_m[c,j]; opp count = Ao[j] - flips[c,j]
    my_after = A1[None, :] + adj_m.astype(np.int64)
    opp_after = Ao[None, :] - flips.astype(np.int64)

    # empty neighbours of j excluding c: E[j] - adj_m[c,j] (c is empty before the claim)
    empty_other = E[None, :] - adj_m.astype(np.int64)

    # recapturable: flipped and opponent can reach a flip with one empty neighbour e != c
    recapturable = flips & (empty_other >= 1) & ((opp_after + 1) >= my_after)

    G = (flips * pts[None, :]).sum(axis=1)
    R = (recapturable * pts[None, :]).sum(axis=1)

    return (G - R) / 15.0
